clue.text: Endorse bill for Scotch

definitions.meaning: marking a settled bill means writing the word for settlement on it
to scotch a plan is to finish it off for good

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: stamping a bill as settled, and idiomatically ending something completely.

clue.text: Fastidious, making short film on Bluegrass State

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State, has the postal abbreviation KY

explanation.surface: Someone fussy makes a brief documentary about Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the film word sits above the state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is hard to please and choosy.

clue.text: It's fine to make a search, but a bit misguided!

definitions.text: It's fine to make a search, but a bit misguided!

parts.words: It's fine to make a search, but a bit misguided!
parts.note: the familiar search tool is the fine-tooth kind; the clue teases that the usual phrase attaches 'fine' to the wrong word

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that searching is fine but slightly wrong-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb with closely set teeth is used for a meticulous search, as in going over something carefully.

clue.text: Writer's taken sort of oath, to keep university den up

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so the university letter goes inside
a sort of oath is a loose version of it, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word for den is written bottom to top

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: An author has sworn some vow and agreed to hold a college study room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is an adjective here, not a possessive: it means belonging to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to an author, so it means belonging to a writer.

clue.text: Have reservations about making progress here

definitions.text: Have reservations about making progress here

parts.words: Have reservations about making progress here
parts.note: doubts are not meant: a central reservation is the strip dividing a major road, and traffic progresses along either side

explanation.surface: Someone is doubtful about advancing in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the central reservation is the barrier strip between the two halves of a divided highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A road split by a central strip into two separate carriageways is where drivers travel beside such reservations.

clue.text: Correctly ascertaining which train to take?

definitions.text: Correctly ascertaining which train to take?

parts.words: Correctly ascertaining which train to take?
parts.note: the idiom for proceeding correctly is read literally as choosing the proper railway line

explanation.surface: A traveller works out which train to board.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means progressing in a way likely to succeed, which literally means picking the proper railway line.

clue.text: Physician's attempt to introduce himself to non-English tipple?

definitions.text: Physician's attempt to introduce himself to non-English tipple?

parts.words: Physician's attempt to introduce himself to non-English tipple?
parts.note: a doctor in broken English might say '...', which sounds like a French red wine from Bordeaux

explanation.surface: A doctor tries clumsily to introduce himself in a foreign bar.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a red wine region of Bordeaux, so a French drink rather than an English one.

clue.text: Wildly enthusiastic Scot touring another part of UK

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the Scot surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the UK besides Scotland

explanation.surface: An excited Scotsman travels round Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied, excessively energetic behaviour is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Sketch has been pinched

definitions.meaning: something sketched has been pictured with pencil
a pinched face is gaunt and strained

explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of the verb for sketching also means haggard, as in a tired face.

clue.text: Sweet about enemy's overthrow? I can't accept that

indicators.note: about means around, so the sweet wraps the reversed enemy

parts.note: a comfit is a sugar-coated sweet

indicators.note: an overthrown enemy is turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A dessert tells of an enemy's downfall, and someone is incredulous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like the definition but is the container; the exclamation at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a scornful expression of disbelief, like 'pull the other one'.

clue.text: Oddball' actor rejected excellent part in Europe

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric, so the letters of actor are jumbled
rejected means sent back, so the word for excellent is reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An eccentric performer turned down a superb role somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddball' makes CROAT from ACTOR; 'rejected' turns AI into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country, one region of the continent.

clue.text: With cat around, close part of hi-fi system

indicators.note: around tells us the cat surrounds the word for close

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
near means close

explanation.surface: A record player has a cat prowling nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: On a record player this pivoting arm holds the stylus over the disc.

clue.text: Travels about with this hooligan

definitions.meaning: Gulliver's Travels features a brutish race of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Swift's brutish humanoids gave their name to any boorish lout.

clue.text: Notes increasing level of noise

parts.note: musical notes marked to grow gradually louder

explanation.surface: Someone observes that the din is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction marks a gradual rise in volume.

clue.text: May French soldiers invading find original inhabitant?

indicators.note: invading means getting inside, so the soldiers go into the French month

parts.note: mai is French for the month of May
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops occupying a French territory in May come upon a native.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polynesian people of New Zealand were its first settlers.

clue.text: Crowd I was in front of is encroaching, ready for conflict

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: encroaching means intruding, so is pushes into the word for led

parts.note: led means was in front

explanation.surface: Someone pushing ahead of a crowd finds it closing in on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops called up and prepared for war are mustered.

clue.text: Saved from a heavy fall?

parts.note: the heavy fall is a downpour, not a tumble

explanation.surface: Someone is rescued from a nasty tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof material protects one against showers.

clue.text: Pay, after Tom perhaps appears to dither

indicators.note: after puts the pay word behind the cat

parts.note: a tomcat is an example of a pussy
to foot a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates after a cat seems to want paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act cautiously and noncommittally, to waver.

clue.text: Prepared to take the heat, staying in the kitchen?

definitions.text: Prepared to take the heat, staying in the kitchen?

parts.words: Prepared to take the heat, staying in the kitchen?
parts.note: the saying about getting out of the kitchen if you can't stand the heat is turned to food ready to be cooked

explanation.surface: Someone who copes with pressure stays in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sold prepared needs only cooking in the oven.

clue.text: Robert's partnering Vivien in Olympic event

parts.note: Bob is short for Robert, with the 's
Vivien Leigh, the actress

explanation.surface: Robert is dancing with Vivien at the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a steerable sled down an ice run is a Winter Games sport.

clue.text: In street, shelter — from this?

indicators.note: In tells us the shelter word sits inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: lee is shelter from wind

explanation.surface: Out in the street, someone looks for cover from bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy rain is the sort of weather one takes cover from.

clue.text: I'll get him to sort out publicity

indicators.note: sorting out means rearranging, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A threat to deal with some troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public eye is being in the glare of attention.

clue.text: Police arresting a number "with intent'

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the police enclose the other letters

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
N is used for number in algebra

explanation.surface: Officers detain someone for a deliberate offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on purpose was intended.

clue.text: Sweet bread

explanation.definitionFit: British slang gives both a lollipop and cash.

clue.text: Maybe gets out of a county

definitions.meaning: in cricket a yorker can bowl a batsman out

explanation.definitionFit: A bowler dismisses a batter with a ball pitched at the feet; also short for Yorkshire, an English county.

clue.text: Almost finalised check on satisfactory part of crop

indicators.note: almost finished means losing the final letter

parts.note: to stop is to check
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A nearly completed inspection of the harvest is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost finalised' takes P off STOP, leaving STO.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of sheaves stood upright in a harvest field.

clue.text: Reluctantly accept a flier

definitions.meaning: to ... an insult is to put up with it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means tolerate without protest, the noun a forked-tailed bird.

clue.text: Fuss about half-forgotten vocalist, for starters?

indicators.note: about places the fuss around the partial singer

parts.note: ado means fuss

indicators.note: half of the word is dropped, keeping the opening half

explanation.surface: A fuss is made about a singer who is half forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: an avocado is a typical first course, hence 'for starters'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is a classic first course at dinner.

clue.text: So pointillism appeared rather eccentric

definitions.meaning: pointillist paintings are made of dots

explanation.definitionFit: Covered with spots and also a bit crazy.

clue.text: Rabbiting, yet crashing into pair of oxen

indicators.note: crashing into places the jumbled letters inside the oxen
a pair means two of the ox word

parts.note: yak is a Himalayan ox

indicators.note: crashing suggests wreckage, so the letters of yet are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone chatters, crashing into two oxen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' turns YET into ETY; 'pair of' doubles YAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean nonstop idle chatter; rabbiting is British slang for talking on.
